objects.description: leveldb::Slice is an immutable, lightweight view over a contiguous byte sequence backed by external storage. It stores a const char* pointer and a size, provides read-only accessors, comparisons, prefix removal, and conversion to std::string. The lifetime of the referenced data must outlive the Slice. Thread-safe for concurrent const operations; non-const operations require external synchronization. No ownership or memory management is performed by Slice.

Represents the outcome of an operation in LevelDB. A default-constructed Status denotes success (OK). Non-OK statuses carry an error code and message stored in an internal heap-allocated byte array. Provides factory methods for common error types (NotFound, Corruption, NotSupported, InvalidArgument, IOError), query methods (ok, IsNotFound, etc.), and string conversion. Copying performs deep copy of the internal state; moving transfers ownership. Thread-safe for concurrent const access; external synchronization required if any thread may call non-const methods. Destruction frees the internal state array.

Abstract interface defining a total order over leveldb::Slice keys. Implementations must be thread-safe. Provides three-way comparison and optional key-shortening hooks used to reduce index sizes. The destructor is virtual. No ownership semantics are specified here; instances are typically long-lived and shared.

Forward-declared value-semantic type representing a non-owning reference to a byte sequence. Only a forward declaration is present in this header; definition is elsewhere. Used as the key type for Comparator methods.

Enumeration of per-block compression algorithms used by LevelDB when writing and reading data blocks. Values are part of the on-disk format and must remain stable.

Configuration struct for opening a LevelDB database, controlling behavior, performance, compression, caching, file sizes, and filter policy. Constructed with default values and then passed to DB::Open. Some fields reference other types (Comparator, Env, Cache, Logger, FilterPolicy) that are forward-declared here.
Options that control read operations, including checksum verification, cache behavior, and an optional Snapshot to provide a read-consistent view.
Options that control write operations, primarily whether each write should be synchronously flushed to durable storage (sync).

Abstract interface for iterating over a sequence of key/value pairs from a LevelDB data source (e.g., a table or database). Implementations provide forward/backward navigation, seek, and access to current key/value and status. Thread-safe for concurrent const methods; non-const methods require external synchronization if used concurrently. Also supports registering cleanup callbacks invoked on destruction.

A batch container for atomic write operations to a LevelDB DB. It records Put and Delete operations and can be iterated with a user-provided Handler. Multiple const callers are thread-safe; non-const access requires external synchronization. The internal representation is an implementation-defined string buffer rep_. Construction/destruction are declared here; definitions are in the implementation file.
Abstract callback interface used to iterate through a WriteBatch's contents. Implementations receive Put and Delete events for each operation in order.

Abstract interface to OS-like services (filesystem, threading, time) used by LevelDB. Provides factory methods for file abstractions, directory and file management, locking, background work scheduling, threading, and timing. Implementations must be thread-safe. Default() returns a shared singleton owned by LevelDB and must not be deleted.
Abstract interface for sequentially reading a file. Not thread-safe; requires external synchronization. Provides Read and Skip operations.
Abstract interface for random-access (read-only) file I/O. Safe for concurrent use by multiple threads. Single Read method with offset.
Abstract interface for buffered sequential writing to a file. Provides Append, Close, Flush, and Sync operations. Not specified as thread-safe; intended for single-writer access.
Abstract interface for logging. Provides a vprintf-style Logv method. Used by Env::NewLogger and helper Log().
Opaque handle identifying a file lock acquired via Env::LockFile. Lifetime managed by Env; users should not construct directly and must release via Env::UnlockFile.
Concrete wrapper that forwards all Env methods to an underlying target Env, allowing selective override via subclassing. Holds a non-owning pointer to target Env.

Abstract interface for a thread-safe cache in leveldb supporting insertion, lookup, release, erasure, id allocation, pruning, and reporting of total charge. It is reference-counted via opaque Handle objects returned by Insert/Lookup and must be subclassed to provide concrete behavior. Destructor virtual; copy/assign deleted.

Abstract interface for building and querying on-disk filters used by LevelDB (e.g., Bloom filters). Implementations summarize a set of keys into a compact byte string (CreateFilter) and can test whether a key may be present (KeyMayMatch). Name identifies the encoding version. Destructor is virtual; instances are typically created via factory helpers and deleted by callers.

Immutable, thread-safe sorted map from strings to strings stored in an SSTable file. Provides APIs to open a table from a RandomAccessFile, create iterators, estimate key offsets, and perform internal lookups with optional filter checks. Lifetime: constructed via Open(), destroyed via destructor. Not copyable. Requires the underlying file to stay alive while the Table exists. Internally uses a Rep struct (opaque here) to hold state and helper methods to read metadata and filters.

Public builder class for creating an immutable LevelDB Table (SSTable) and writing it to a provided WritableFile. It enforces sorted key insertion, supports option changes with restrictions, can flush pending entries, and finalizes or abandons construction. Non-copyable; manages internal state via a private Rep implementation. Destructor requires either Finish() or Abandon() to have been called.

Abstract handle representing an immutable snapshot of a DB state. Thread-safe to access concurrently. Only a protected virtual destructor is declared here; instances are obtained and released via DB::GetSnapshot and DB::ReleaseSnapshot, not constructed directly.

Represents a half-open key interval [start, limit). Used with DB APIs such as GetApproximateSizes and CompactRange to specify key ranges. Holds two Slice members referencing user-provided memory; lifetime of underlying data must outlive Range usage.

Abstract interface for a LevelDB key-value store. Provides CRUD operations, batched writes, iteration, snapshots, properties, approximate size queries, and compaction. Instances are created via DB::Open and deleted by the caller. All methods are thread-safe to call concurrently unless otherwise specified.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::Slice
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an empty Slice that refers to no external data (data_ points to a static empty string, size_ is 0). Typically used to initialize a Slice before assigning it to real data.
requirements: Resulting Slice is empty (size() == 0).
Thread-safety: const methods may be called concurrently; if any thread may call non-const methods (e.g., clear(), remove_prefix(), or assignment), external synchronization is required.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::Slice
functions.description: Constructs a Slice that refers to the memory range d[0..n-1] without taking ownership. No copy is made; the Slice is just a view.
requirements: If n > 0, d must be a valid, non-null pointer to at least n bytes of readable memory.
The referenced external storage must outlive all uses of this Slice; do not use the Slice after the underlying memory is deallocated or modified.
The memory need not be null-terminated.
Thread-safety: const methods may be called concurrently; if any thread may call non-const methods on the same Slice, external synchronization is required.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::Slice
functions.description: Constructs a Slice that refers to the contents of the provided std::string without copying. The Slice points into s.data() for s.size() bytes.
requirements: The std::string instance s (or an equivalent buffer with identical lifetime) must remain alive and unmodified for the entire duration the Slice is used; otherwise the Slice will dangle or observe changed data.
No ownership is transferred; the Slice is a view.
Thread-safety: const methods may be called concurrently; if any thread may call non-const methods on the same Slice, external synchronization is required.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::Slice
functions.description: Constructs a Slice from a null-terminated C string. Computes size as strlen(s) and refers to s[0..strlen(s)-1]. The data is not copied.
requirements: s must be a valid, non-null pointer to a null-terminated C string.
The underlying storage pointed to by s must outlive all uses of the Slice.
Thread-safety: const methods may be called concurrently; if any thread may call non-const methods on the same Slice, external synchronization is required.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::Slice
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a new Slice that refers to the same external data as the source Slice. Shallow copy; no data is duplicated.
requirements: Source Slice may be empty or non-empty; copied Slice will reference the same underlying memory and share lifetime requirements.
The referenced external storage must outlive all uses of both Slices.
Thread-safety: copying itself is not thread-safe if other threads mutate the same Slice; synchronize if any non-const operations may occur.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Makes this Slice refer to the same external data as another Slice. Shallow assignment; no data is copied.
requirements: Both the existing and assigned-from Slices reference external storage; after assignment, this Slice shares the same underlying memory as the source.
The referenced external storage must outlive all uses of the assigned-to Slice.
Not thread-safe with concurrent mutations; if any thread may call non-const methods on the same Slice instance, use external synchronization.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::data
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the beginning of the referenced data. May be null only for an empty Slice that was constructed with a null pointer and n == 0; otherwise points to valid memory.
requirements: Caller must not access beyond size() bytes starting at data().
The underlying memory must remain valid for the duration of use.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::size
functions.description: Returns the number of bytes referenced by this Slice.
requirements: None beyond the Slice being a valid object.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::empty
functions.description: Returns true if the Slice references zero bytes (size() == 0).
requirements: None beyond the Slice being a valid object.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::begin
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the first byte of the referenced data, equivalent to data().
requirements: Do not read past end(); only dereference if size() > 0.
Underlying storage must remain valid for the duration of use.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::end
functions.description: Returns a pointer one past the last byte of the referenced data (data() + size()). Suitable for half-open range iteration [begin(), end()).
requirements: Pointer arithmetic assumes data() points to at least size() bytes of valid memory.
Do not dereference the returned pointer unless size() > 0 and you know it points within the valid range.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::operator[]
functions.description: Returns the n-th byte of the referenced data by value. Asserts that n < size().
requirements: n must satisfy 0 <= n < size(); otherwise behavior triggers an assertion failure in debug builds and is undefined in release builds.
Underlying storage must be valid for at least n+1 bytes.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::clear
functions.description: Makes this Slice empty by setting its size to 0 and pointing data() to a static empty string literal.
requirements: Not thread-safe with concurrent access; if any thread may access the same Slice concurrently, external synchronization is required when calling this non-const method.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::remove_prefix
functions.description: Drops the first n bytes from this Slice by advancing the internal data pointer and reducing size. Does not modify the underlying storage.
requirements: Requires n <= size(); the function asserts this precondition.
After the call, the Slice will reference the subrange [old_data + n, old_data + size).
Not thread-safe with concurrent access; if any thread may access the same Slice concurrently, external synchronization is required when calling this non-const method.
Underlying storage must remain valid for the new range.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::ToString
functions.description: Returns a std::string containing a copy of the referenced data. Safe to use independently of the lifetime of the original storage.
requirements: Allocates and copies size() bytes; may throw std::bad_alloc if allocation fails (standard library behavior).
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::compare
functions.description: Three-way lexicographical comparison of two Slices using memcmp() on the common prefix, then lengths. Returns <0 if *this < b, 0 if equal, >0 if *this > b.
requirements: Both Slices must refer to valid memory for their sizes; memcmp reads up to min(size(), b.size()) bytes from each.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Slice::starts_with
functions.description: Returns true if x is a prefix of this Slice (size() >= x.size() and memcmp(data(), x.data(), x.size()) == 0).
requirements: Both Slices must refer to valid memory for their sizes.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::operator==
functions.signature: bool leveldb::operator==(const leveldb::Slice& x, const leveldb::Slice& y)
functions.description: Equality comparison. Returns true if x and y have the same size and identical byte contents (memcmp over x.size() bytes).
requirements: x and y must each refer to valid memory for their sizes; memcmp reads x.size() bytes from both.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::operator!=
functions.signature: bool leveldb::operator!=(const leveldb::Slice& x, const leveldb::Slice& y)
functions.description: Inequality comparison. Logical negation of operator==.
requirements: x and y must each refer to valid memory for their sizes.
May be called concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Status::Status
functions.description: Default constructor that creates a success (OK) status with no error state. Use when an operation succeeds or as an initial value.
requirements: No special preconditions.

functions.name: leveldb::Status::Status
functions.description: Copy constructor. Produces a deep copy of rhs, duplicating its internal state so the new Status is independent of rhs.
requirements: rhs must refer to a valid leveldb::Status object.

Threading: copying is a non-const operation on the destination; if the same Status object is accessed by multiple threads and any may perform non-const operations (like assignment), external synchronization is required (per class comment).

functions.name: leveldb::Status::Status
functions.description: Move constructor. Transfers ownership of rhs's internal state to this object, leaving rhs in an empty/OK state.
requirements: rhs must be a valid leveldb::Status object; after the call, rhs is left in an OK/empty state and should not be relied on to hold the previous error.
Threading: moving affects both this and rhs and is non-const; if shared across threads, external synchronization is required (per class comment).

functions.name: leveldb::Status::~Status
functions.description: Destructor that releases any internally allocated error state. Safe to destroy an OK status or any error status.

functions.name: leveldb::Status::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces this Status with a deep copy of rhs, freeing any existing internal state.
requirements: rhs must refer to a valid leveldb::Status object.
Self-assignment is safe.
Threading: operator= is a non-const operation; if multiple threads access the same Status object and any may call operator=, all such access must be externally synchronized (per class comment).

functions.name: leveldb::Status::operator=
functions.description: Move assignment operator. Swaps internal state with rhs, effectively transferring rhs's state to this object and leaving rhs in an OK/empty state.
requirements: rhs must be a valid leveldb::Status object; after the call, rhs is left in an OK/empty state.
Threading: operator= is a non-const operation; if multiple threads access the same Status object and any may call operator=, all such access must be externally synchronized (per class comment).

functions.name: leveldb::Comparator::~Comparator
functions.description: Virtual destructor for leveldb::Comparator. Enables safe deletion of comparator implementations via a base-class pointer and proper cleanup of derived resources. Typically used when custom Comparator implementations are owned by the caller or a DB instance.
requirements: Only destroy Comparator instances that you own (do not delete the pointer returned by leveldb::BytewiseComparator()).
Object must have been fully constructed before destruction.

functions.name: leveldb::Comparator::Compare
functions.signature: virtual int Compare(const leveldb::Slice& a, const leveldb::Slice& b) const = 0;
functions.description: Three-way comparison of two keys. Returns <0 if a<b, 0 if a==b, >0 if a>b, establishing a total order over Slice keys. Used by LevelDB for ordering in tables and the database. Implementations must be consistent and thread-safe.
requirements: Must be callable concurrently from multiple threads; implementation must be thread-safe.
Must define a strict weak ordering that is consistent and total for all possible key values represented by leveldb::Slice.
Must not modify inputs a or b.
Return value semantics: negative if a<b, zero if equal, positive if a>b.
Inputs a and b must refer to valid Slice objects for the duration of the call.

functions.name: leveldb::Comparator::Name
functions.description: Returns a stable, implementation-identifying name for the comparator. Used by LevelDB to detect comparator mismatches across database instances. Change the name when the comparator’s ordering semantics change.
requirements: Returned pointer must remain valid for the lifetime of the Comparator object (and typically process-lifetime if static).
Names starting with "leveldb." are reserved and must not be used by clients.
If the comparator’s ordering changes in any way that could reorder keys, the returned name must change accordingly.
Function must be callable concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Comparator::FindShortestSeparator
functions.signature: virtual void FindShortestSeparator(std::string* start, const leveldb::Slice& limit) const = 0;
functions.description: Optionally shortens *start to a string in the half-open interval [*start, limit) to reduce internal index sizes, if *start < limit. Simple implementations may leave *start unchanged. Used by LevelDB during internal structure construction.
requirements: start must be a non-null pointer to a valid std::string.
limit must be a valid Slice for the duration of the call.
If *start >= limit, the method may leave *start unchanged; the result (if changed) must still satisfy *start < limit and be >= original *start.
Function must be callable concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Comparator::FindShortSuccessor
functions.description: Optionally shortens or modifies *key to a short string that is >= the original *key, typically to reduce internal index sizes. Simple implementations may leave *key unchanged. Used in LevelDB for optimizing separators/successors.
requirements: key must be a non-null pointer to a valid std::string.
If modified, the result must be >= the original value of *key.
Function must be callable concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.description: Reports whether the iterator is currently positioned at a valid key/value pair. Use this to test iterator state before accessing key() or value() or after movement/seek operations.
requirements: May be called concurrently by multiple threads without external synchronization (const method).

functions.name: leveldb::Iterator::SeekToFirst
functions.description: Positions the iterator at the first key in the source. After the call, Valid() is true iff the source is not empty.
requirements: External synchronization is required if any thread may call non-const methods on the same iterator (non-const method).
No other preconditions.

functions.name: leveldb::Iterator::SeekToLast
functions.description: Positions the iterator at the last key in the source. After the call, Valid() is true iff the source is not empty.
requirements: External synchronization is required if any thread may call non-const methods on the same iterator (non-const method).
No other preconditions.

functions.name: leveldb::Iterator::Seek
functions.description: Positions the iterator at the first key that is at or past the specified target key. After the call, Valid() is true iff the source contains such an entry.
requirements: Argument target: must reference a valid leveldb::Slice during the call.
External synchronization is required if any thread may call non-const methods on the same iterator (non-const method).

functions.name: leveldb::Iterator::Next
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next entry. After the call, Valid() is true iff the iterator was not positioned at the last entry.
requirements: REQUIRES: Valid() must be true before calling Next().
External synchronization is required if any thread may call non-const methods on the same iterator (non-const method).

functions.name: leveldb::Iterator::Prev
functions.description: Moves the iterator to the previous entry. After the call, Valid() is true iff the iterator was not positioned at the first entry.
requirements: REQUIRES: Valid() must be true before calling Prev().
External synchronization is required if any thread may call non-const methods on the same iterator (non-const method).

functions.name: leveldb::Iterator::key
functions.description: Returns the key for the current entry as a Slice. The underlying storage backing the returned Slice remains valid only until the next modification of the iterator (e.g., Seek/Next/Prev) or destruction.
requirements: REQUIRES: Valid() must be true before calling key().
The returned Slice’s underlying storage must not be accessed after the iterator is modified; copy the data if it must outlive the iterator’s next modification or destruction.
May be called concurrently by multiple threads without external synchronization (const method).

functions.name: leveldb::Iterator::value
functions.description: Returns the value for the current entry as a Slice. The underlying storage backing the returned Slice remains valid only until the next modification of the iterator (e.g., Seek/Next/Prev) or destruction.
requirements: REQUIRES: Valid() must be true before calling value().
The returned Slice’s underlying storage must not be accessed after the iterator is modified; copy the data if it must outlive the iterator’s next modification or destruction.
May be called concurrently by multiple threads without external synchronization (const method).

functions.name: leveldb::Iterator::status
functions.description: Returns an error Status if an error has occurred during iteration, otherwise returns ok. Use to detect deferred or non-fatal errors after iteration operations.
requirements: May be called concurrently by multiple threads without external synchronization (const method).
No preconditions.

functions.name: leveldb::Iterator::RegisterCleanup
functions.signature: void leveldb::Iterator::RegisterCleanup(leveldb::Iterator::CleanupFunction function, void* arg1, void* arg2)
functions.description: Registers a cleanup callback (function, arg1, arg2) that will be invoked when this iterator is destroyed. Multiple callbacks may be registered; they are maintained internally in a singly linked list.
requirements: function must be a valid function pointer (non-null); it will be called as function(arg1, arg2) during iterator destruction.
Callbacks must be safe to execute at iterator destruction time and must not rely on the iterator still being valid.
External synchronization is required if any thread may call non-const methods on the same iterator (non-const method).

functions.name: leveldb::NewEmptyIterator
functions.description: Creates and returns an iterator that yields no entries (always invalid). Useful as a placeholder or for error/empty results where an Iterator is required by an API.
requirements: Caller must treat the returned object as an Iterator supporting the standard iterator interface; Valid() will be false, and key()/value() require Valid() and therefore must not be called.
Thread-safety follows the standard Iterator rules (const methods may be called concurrently; non-const methods require external synchronization).
Ownership/lifetime: not explicitly documented in this header; typical LevelDB pattern is that the caller is responsible for deleting the returned Iterator when finished (inferred).

functions.name: leveldb::NewErrorIterator
functions.description: Creates and returns an empty iterator that carries the specified status. The iterator yields no entries (Valid() is false), and status() returns the provided status, enabling APIs to return an iterator alongside an error.
requirements: Argument status: should be a valid leveldb::Status object; no specific error requirement is stated.
Caller must not call key()/value() since the iterator is empty (Valid() will be false).
Thread-safety follows the standard Iterator rules (const methods may be called concurrently; non-const methods require external synchronization).
Ownership/lifetime: not explicitly documented in this header; typical LevelDB pattern is that the caller is responsible for deleting the returned Iterator when finished (inferred).

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::Handler::~Handler
functions.description: Virtual destructor for WriteBatch::Handler. Enables safe deletion through a base-pointer to Handler implementations used when iterating a WriteBatch.
requirements: Must be implemented or linked from LevelDB; user subclasses do not need to override it.
No concurrent calls that race with object destruction.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::Handler::Put
functions.signature: virtual void leveldb::WriteBatch::Handler::Put(const leveldb::Slice& key, const leveldb::Slice& value) = 0
functions.description: Pure-virtual callback invoked for each Put operation during WriteBatch iteration. Implement this in a subclass to process key/value insertions encountered by WriteBatch::Iterate.
requirements: Must be implemented by any concrete Handler subclass before passing it to WriteBatch::Iterate.
Handler implementation must tolerate being called multiple times in order of the batch.
The provided Slices reference external memory; if data must be retained after return, copy it.
Must not assume null-termination; Slices may contain arbitrary binary data.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::Handler::Delete
functions.description: Pure-virtual callback invoked for each Delete operation during WriteBatch iteration. Implement this in a subclass to process deletions encountered by WriteBatch::Iterate.
requirements: Must be implemented by any concrete Handler subclass before passing it to WriteBatch::Iterate.
Handler implementation must tolerate being called multiple times in order of the batch.
The provided Slice references external memory; if the key must be retained after return, copy it.
Must not assume null-termination; Slice may contain arbitrary binary data.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::WriteBatch
functions.description: Default constructor. Creates an empty WriteBatch to which updates can be added and later applied atomically to a DB or iterated via a Handler.
requirements: If the same WriteBatch instance may be accessed by multiple threads and any thread calls a non-const method (e.g., Put/Delete/Clear/Append), callers must provide external synchronization.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::WriteBatch
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a new WriteBatch by copying all buffered updates from another batch.
requirements: Copying runs in O(source size) time (per documentation).
If the same WriteBatch instance may be accessed by multiple threads and any thread calls a non-const method, callers must provide external synchronization.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::~WriteBatch
functions.description: Destructor that releases resources held by the WriteBatch.
requirements: Do not destroy the object concurrently with any other access to it.
If shared among threads, ensure external synchronization during destruction.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::operator=
functions.description: Copy assignment operator. Replaces the contents of this WriteBatch with a copy of another batch’s buffered updates.
requirements: Assignment runs in O(source size) time (implied by copying semantics).
If the same WriteBatch instance may be accessed by multiple threads and any thread calls a non-const method, callers must provide external synchronization.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::Put
functions.signature: void leveldb::WriteBatch::Put(const leveldb::Slice& key, const leveldb::Slice& value)
functions.description: Adds a Put operation to the batch, storing the mapping key->value when the batch is applied. Operations are applied in the order added.
requirements: key and value are treated as byte sequences; they need not be null-terminated and may contain arbitrary binary data.
The method copies the key/value into the batch; the input Slices need only remain valid for the duration of the call (inferred from LevelDB Slice usage and WriteBatch encoding).
If the same WriteBatch instance may be accessed by multiple threads and any thread calls a non-const method, callers must provide external synchronization.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::Delete
functions.description: Adds a Delete operation to the batch. If the database contains a mapping for key, it will be removed when the batch is applied; otherwise, no effect. Operations are applied in the order added.
requirements: key is a byte sequence; it need not be null-terminated and may contain arbitrary binary data.
The method copies the key into the batch; the input Slice need only remain valid for the duration of the call (inferred from LevelDB Slice usage and WriteBatch encoding).
If the same WriteBatch instance may be accessed by multiple threads and any thread calls a non-const method, callers must provide external synchronization.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::Clear
functions.description: Removes all buffered updates from the batch, leaving it empty.
requirements: If the same WriteBatch instance may be accessed by multiple threads and any thread calls a non-const method, callers must provide external synchronization.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::ApproximateSize
functions.description: Returns an implementation-tied estimate of the space impact of this batch’s operations. Intended for LevelDB usage metrics; value may change across releases.
requirements: May be called concurrently with other const operations; if any thread may call a non-const method on the same instance, callers must provide external synchronization for all accesses (per class-level threading note).

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::Append
functions.description: Appends all operations from source to this batch. More efficient than iterating with a Handler that replays into this batch. Runs in O(source size) time.
requirements: source must be a valid WriteBatch object.
If the same WriteBatch instance may be accessed by multiple threads and any thread calls a non-const method, callers must provide external synchronization.
Appended operations will preserve the order: existing operations remain before the appended ones.

functions.name: leveldb::WriteBatch::Iterate
functions.description: Invokes handler->Put/Delete for each operation in the batch in the order they were added. Use this to process or replay the batch’s contents without applying them to a DB.
requirements: handler must be a valid, non-null pointer to an object whose class derives from WriteBatch::Handler and implements Put and Delete.
Handler callbacks may be invoked many times; implementations must be reentrant with respect to repeated calls by the same thread.
Do not modify the WriteBatch from within the handler calls to avoid undefined behavior (not specified in the header; conservative best practice).
Caller should check the returned Status and handle errors accordingly.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::Default
functions.description: Returns a process-wide default Env implementation for the current OS. Intended for clients who do not need a custom Env. The returned pointer is owned by leveldb and must not be deleted by the caller.
requirements: Caller must not delete or free the returned Env pointer; ownership remains with leveldb.
The returned Env may be used concurrently from multiple threads (Env implementations are thread-safe).

functions.name: leveldb::Env::NewSequentialFile
functions.signature: virtual leveldb::Status leveldb::Env::NewSequentialFile(const std::string& fname, leveldb::SequentialFile** result) = 0;
functions.description: Creates a SequentialFile for reading the named file sequentially. On success, stores a new SequentialFile* in *result and returns OK; on failure, stores nullptr in *result and returns non-OK (NotFound if the file does not exist). The returned file object is intended for single-threaded access at a time.
requirements: fname must name an existing file to succeed; implementations should return NotFound if it does not exist.
Caller must provide a valid non-null pointer for result; on success it receives ownership of the created SequentialFile object per Env contract.
The returned SequentialFile must be externally synchronized by the caller if accessed (the interface requires external synchronization).
Caller must check the returned Status before using *result.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::NewRandomAccessFile
functions.signature: virtual leveldb::Status leveldb::Env::NewRandomAccessFile(const std::string& fname, leveldb::RandomAccessFile** result) = 0;
functions.description: Creates a RandomAccessFile for random reads of the named file. On success, stores a new RandomAccessFile* in *result and returns OK; on failure, stores nullptr in *result and returns non-OK (NotFound if the file does not exist). The returned file supports concurrent access by multiple threads.
requirements: fname must refer to an existing file to succeed; NotFound should be returned otherwise.
Caller must provide a valid non-null pointer for result and must check the returned Status before use.
RandomAccessFile instances may be used concurrently from multiple threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::NewWritableFile
functions.signature: virtual leveldb::Status leveldb::Env::NewWritableFile(const std::string& fname, leveldb::WritableFile** result) = 0;
functions.description: Creates a new file for writing at the given path, deleting any existing file with the same name. On success, returns a WritableFile* in *result and OK; on failure, stores nullptr in *result and returns non-OK. Intended for single-threaded access at a time.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid non-null result pointer and check the returned Status before using *result.
Existing file at fname will be deleted or truncated per Env implementation—callers should not expect preservation of prior contents.
WritableFile is intended to be accessed by only one thread at a time unless externally synchronized by the caller.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::NewAppendableFile
functions.signature: virtual leveldb::Status leveldb::Env::NewAppendableFile(const std::string& fname, leveldb::WritableFile** result);
functions.description: Opens an existing file for appending or creates a new file if it does not exist. On success, sets *result to a WritableFile and returns OK; on failure, sets *result to nullptr and returns non-OK. Some Env implementations may not support append and can return an IsNotSupportedError.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid non-null result pointer and check the returned Status before using *result.
The returned WritableFile should be accessed by only one thread at a time.
Caller must handle the possibility of IsNotSupportedError and be prepared to fall back (e.g., by rewriting).

functions.name: leveldb::Env::FileExists
functions.description: Checks whether a file with the given name exists and returns true if and only if it does.
requirements: fname should be a valid path in the Env's filesystem namespace.

functions.description: Lists direct children (names relative to dir) of the specified directory. On success, populates *result with the names and returns OK. On failure, returns non-OK. Any original contents of *result are discarded.
requirements: dir must reference an existing directory for a successful listing.
Caller must pass a valid non-null result pointer; its prior contents will be dropped.
Caller must check the returned Status before using the results.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::RemoveFile
functions.description: Deletes the named file. This is the modern replacement for the deprecated DeleteFile. The default implementation calls DeleteFile for backward compatibility with legacy Env implementations.
requirements: Caller must pass a valid path to a file within the Env's filesystem namespace.
Caller must check the returned Status to determine success or reason for failure.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::DeleteFile
functions.description: Deprecated file deletion API. The default implementation forwards to RemoveFile to support legacy code. Modern callers should use RemoveFile instead.
requirements: Caller should migrate to RemoveFile; this method may be removed in a future release.
Caller must check the returned Status to determine success or failure.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::CreateDir
functions.description: Creates the specified directory.
requirements: dirname must be a valid path in the Env's namespace and must not conflict with an existing non-directory entry.
Caller must check the returned Status.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::RemoveDir
functions.description: Deletes the specified directory. Modern replacement for deprecated DeleteDir. The default implementation calls DeleteDir for backward compatibility.
requirements: dirname must identify a directory in the Env's namespace.

Caller must check the returned Status.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::DeleteDir
functions.description: Deprecated directory deletion API. The default implementation forwards to RemoveDir. Modern callers should use RemoveDir instead.
requirements: Caller should prefer RemoveDir; this method may be removed in a future release.
Caller must check the returned Status.

functions.description: Acquires an interprocess lock on the named file to prevent concurrent DB access by multiple processes. On success, stores a FileLock* in *lock and returns OK. If already locked, fails immediately. May create the file if it does not exist. The lock is automatically released if the process exits.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid non-null lock pointer and check the returned Status before using *lock.
If the file is already locked by another process, the call fails without waiting.
On success, the caller must later call UnlockFile(*lock) exactly once to release the lock.

functions.name: leveldb::Env::UnlockFile
functions.description: Releases a file lock previously obtained via a successful LockFile call.
requirements: lock must have been returned by a successful LockFile call.
lock must not have already been unlocked.
Caller must check the returned Status.

functions.name: leveldb::NewLRUCache
functions.description: Constructs a new Cache instance with a fixed total capacity and a least-recently-used (LRU) eviction policy. Use this to obtain a concrete Cache implementation that can be shared across threads.
requirements: capacity specifies the total cache capacity against which per-entry charges are accounted.
The returned Cache* must eventually be deleted by the owner to release resources (standard C++ ownership).
The resulting Cache may be accessed concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: leveldb::Cache::~Cache
functions.description: Virtual destructor for Cache. Destroys existing entries, invoking the registered deleter(s) for stored entries. Use to ensure proper cleanup when deleting a Cache through a base pointer.
requirements: Should be invoked via object destruction (e.g., delete on a Cache*).
All outstanding handles should be released by callers before destruction to avoid holding entries alive (implied by handle semantics).

functions.name: leveldb::Cache::Insert
functions.signature: virtual leveldb::Cache::Handle* leveldb::Cache::Insert(const leveldb::Slice& key, void* value, size_t charge, void (*deleter)(const leveldb::Slice& key, void* value)) = 0;
functions.description: Inserts a key→value mapping into the cache with the specified charge (cost) against the cache’s capacity. Returns a handle that pins the entry; the caller must release it when finished. When the entry is no longer needed by the cache, the provided deleter is called with the key and value.
requirements: Caller must provide a valid deleter function pointer that can accept (const Slice&, void*) for the inserted entry.
The returned Handle* must be released exactly once via Cache::Release when the caller is done with it.
charge represents this entry’s cost against the cache capacity; its meaning is defined by the cache policy.
key and value must remain valid for the cache’s use until the cache later calls the provided deleter with them (implied by deleter contract).
Thread-safe: may be called concurrently with other Cache operations.

functions.name: leveldb::Cache::Lookup
functions.description: Finds the cache entry for key. Returns a handle that pins the entry if found; otherwise returns nullptr. Callers must release the handle when done.
requirements: If the return value is non-null, the Handle* must be released exactly once via Cache::Release.
May return nullptr if no mapping exists for key; callers must handle this case.
Thread-safe: may be called concurrently with other Cache operations.

functions.name: leveldb::Cache::Release
functions.description: Releases a handle previously returned by Insert or Lookup, decrementing its pin/reference in the cache.
requirements: handle must not have been released before (release exactly once).
handle must have been returned by a method on this Cache instance (*this).
handle must be non-null.
Thread-safe: may be called concurrently with other Cache operations.

functions.name: leveldb::Cache::Value
functions.description: Returns the value pointer associated with a valid, currently held handle obtained from this cache.
requirements: handle must not have been released yet.
handle must have been returned by a method on this Cache instance (*this).
handle must be non-null before calling Value.

functions.name: leveldb::Cache::Erase
functions.description: Removes the cache entry for key if it exists. The underlying entry persists until all outstanding handles to it are released; thereafter the registered deleter is invoked.
requirements: Safe to call even if the key is not present (no-op in that case).
Callers holding handles to the entry must still call Release on those handles.
Thread-safe: may be called concurrently with other Cache operations.

functions.name: leveldb::Cache::NewId
functions.description: Returns a new numeric identifier. Clients sharing a cache can use distinct ids to partition key spaces (e.g., by prefixing keys with the id).
requirements: No specific input requirements; may be called at startup or as needed to obtain unique ids.
Thread-safe: may be called concurrently with other Cache operations.

functions.name: leveldb::Cache::Prune
functions.description: Removes all cache entries that are not actively in use to reduce memory usage. The base implementation does nothing; concrete caches are encouraged to override.
requirements: May be called by memory-constrained applications to prompt reclamation of unused entries.
No guarantee of effect if the implementation does not override the default.

functions.name: leveldb::Cache::TotalCharge
functions.description: Returns an estimate of the sum of charges of all elements currently stored in the cache.
requirements: Callable at any time to observe current cache usage.
Thread-safe: may be called concurrently with other Cache operations.

functions.name: leveldb::FilterPolicy::~FilterPolicy
functions.description: Virtual destructor for FilterPolicy. Releases resources owned by the policy implementation. Typically called when the policy is no longer needed by any database using it.
requirements: Do not use a FilterPolicy instance after its destructor has been invoked.
Ensure no database or component is still using the FilterPolicy at the time of destruction (implied by the lifetime note on NewBloomFilterPolicy).

functions.name: leveldb::FilterPolicy::Name
functions.description: Returns a stable, implementation-specific name for the filter policy. Used to identify filter encodings and detect incompatibilities across versions.
requirements: Must be callable on a valid FilterPolicy instance.
Returned string must remain valid for the lifetime of the policy object (implied by returning const char*).
If the filter encoding changes incompatibly in an implementation, the implementation must change the returned name (requirement for implementers; callers should treat the name as an identifier).

functions.name: leveldb::FilterPolicy::CreateFilter
functions.signature: void leveldb::FilterPolicy::CreateFilter(const leveldb::Slice* keys, int n, std::string* dst) const
functions.description: Appends a compact filter representation summarizing the given ordered list of keys to the destination string. The filter is later used to cheaply test key membership.
requirements: keys must point to an array of at least n leveldb::Slice elements.
n must be non-negative.
The keys[0..n-1] are expected to be ordered according to the user-supplied comparator (as documented).
dst must be a non-null pointer to a valid std::string; the method will append to its existing contents and must not alter its initial contents except by appending.
May be called with duplicate keys in the input array.

functions.name: leveldb::FilterPolicy::KeyMayMatch
functions.signature: bool leveldb::FilterPolicy::KeyMayMatch(const leveldb::Slice& key, const leveldb::Slice& filter) const
functions.description: Tests whether a key may be present according to the provided filter previously produced by CreateFilter(). Returns true if the key was in the original key set; may return true or false for non-members (aiming for low false positives).
requirements: filter must contain the data appended by a preceding call to CreateFilter() from the same FilterPolicy implementation.
key is any valid leveldb::Slice; it need not be ordered.

Return value semantics: true guarantees membership only for keys from the original set; for non-members, the method may return either value, but should strive to return false with high probability (Bloom filter behavior).

functions.name: leveldb::NewBloomFilterPolicy
functions.description: Creates a new Bloom filter policy configured to use approximately the specified number of bits per key. Common value is 10 bits/key (~1% false-positive rate). The returned policy can be supplied to DB options to enable Bloom filtering.
requirements: bits_per_key should be a positive integer (implied by being a count of bits per key).
The returned FilterPolicy* must be deleted by the caller, but only after any database using it has been closed.
Do not use this function if you use a custom comparator that ignores parts of keys; instead provide a custom FilterPolicy with matching semantics.

functions.name: leveldb::Table::Open
functions.signature: static leveldb::Status leveldb::Table::Open(const leveldb::Options& options, leveldb::RandomAccessFile* file, uint64_t file_size, leveldb::Table** table)
functions.description: Opens an immutable, thread-safe Table backed by the bytes in [0..file_size) of the given RandomAccessFile, reading enough metadata to allow lookups and iteration. On success returns an OK Status and stores a newly created Table in *table; on failure returns a non-OK Status and sets *table to nullptr. The Table does not take ownership of the file and relies on it remaining valid for the Table’s lifetime. Typical usage: call Open once per on-disk table/SST and delete the returned Table when finished.
requirements: file must point to a live RandomAccessFile representing the table data, and it must remain valid for the entire lifetime of the returned Table
file_size must describe the byte range [0..file_size) that contains the table; the table is expected to be stored entirely within this range
table must be a non-null pointer to a leveldb::Table* storage location; on success *table is set to a valid Table, on failure *table is set to nullptr
Caller must check the returned Status for success/failure before using *table
Caller owns the returned Table and must delete it when no longer needed
This function does not take ownership of file; the caller remains responsible for the file object’s lifetime

functions.name: leveldb::Table::~Table
functions.description: Destructor for Table. Releases resources associated with the table instance. Use when the table is no longer needed and after all operations/iterators referencing it have completed.
requirements: The Table must not be in use by any thread at the time of destruction (callers must ensure no concurrent accesses during or after ~Table)
The associated RandomAccessFile (passed to Open) may be released after the Table is destroyed

functions.name: leveldb::Table::NewIterator
functions.description: Creates a new iterator over the table’s key/value contents. The returned iterator is initially invalid; the caller must call a Seek method (e.g., SeekToFirst, Seek, SeekToLast) before reading entries. Intended for read-only traversal of an immutable table.
requirements: The returned iterator is initially invalid; the caller must call one of the Seek methods before using it
The Table object must outlive the returned Iterator (the iterator references table data)
Iterator ownership: by LevelDB convention, the caller is responsible for deleting the returned Iterator when finished (not explicitly stated here but consistent with leveldb::Iterator API)
The provided ReadOptions must remain valid for the duration of the call; the iterator’s behavior may depend on these options

functions.name: leveldb::Table::ApproximateOffsetOf
functions.description: Returns an approximate byte offset within the underlying file where the data for the given key begins (or would begin if absent). The offset accounts for file layout effects such as compression and is suitable for coarse positioning or progress estimation; it is not guaranteed exact. The offset of the last key in the table is typically near the file size.
requirements: key must reference a valid Slice during the call
The returned offset is approximate and must not be assumed to be exact or page-aligned
The Table must be valid (not destroyed) for the duration of the call

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::TableBuilder
functions.description: Constructs a TableBuilder that writes a sorted, immutable table to the provided WritableFile using the specified Options. The file is not closed by the builder; the caller must close it after Finish() succeeds. Typical usage: create the builder, call Add() for each key/value in increasing key order, optionally Flush() between groups, then call Finish() (or Abandon() to discard).
requirements: Caller is responsible for closing the WritableFile after a successful Finish().
If multiple threads may access this TableBuilder and any thread may call a non-const method, callers must use external synchronization (per class-level note).
The same TableBuilder instance should be used to build one table; do not reuse after Finish() or Abandon() (implied by API semantics).

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::~TableBuilder
functions.description: Destructor for TableBuilder. Cleans up internal resources. Per the class contract, a TableBuilder must be finalized via Finish() or explicitly discarded via Abandon() before destruction.
requirements: Requires that either Finish() or Abandon() has been called before the object is destroyed (REQUIRES comment).
If multiple threads may access this TableBuilder and any thread may call a non-const method, callers must use external synchronization (per class-level note).

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::ChangeOptions
functions.description: Attempts to change some options of the TableBuilder after construction. Only a subset of option fields are allowed to change dynamically; if any disallowed field differs from the originally provided options, returns a non-ok Status and leaves the builder’s options unchanged.
requirements: Only some Options fields are changeable after construction; if a non-changeable field differs, the function returns an error without changing any fields (per comment).
Callers must check the returned Status for success or failure.
If multiple threads may access this TableBuilder and any thread may call a non-const method, callers must use external synchronization (per class-level note).

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::Add
functions.signature: void leveldb::TableBuilder::Add(const leveldb::Slice& key, const leveldb::Slice& value)
functions.description: Appends a key/value pair to the table under construction. Keys must be provided in strictly increasing order according to the comparator configured in Options. Intended usage: call repeatedly to add entries, then call Finish().
requirements: key must be after any previously added key according to the comparator (REQUIRES comment).
Finish() and Abandon() must not have been called (REQUIRES comment).
If multiple threads may access this TableBuilder and any thread may call a non-const method, callers must use external synchronization (per class-level note).

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::Flush
functions.description: Forces any buffered key/value pairs to be written to the file, ensuring subsequent entries start in a new data block. Intended for advanced use to keep adjacent entries in separate data blocks; most clients do not need this.
requirements: Finish() and Abandon() must not have been called (REQUIRES comment).
If multiple threads may access this TableBuilder and any thread may call a non-const method, callers must use external synchronization (per class-level note).

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::status
functions.description: Returns the current Status of the builder. Returns non-ok if an error has been detected so far. Useful to check for write/build errors after operations like Add() or Flush().
requirements: May be invoked concurrently by multiple threads without external synchronization only if no thread may call a non-const method; otherwise, external synchronization is required (per class-level note).
Callers should check the returned Status before proceeding if errors must be detected early.

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::Finish
functions.description: Finishes building the table, writes any remaining data, and stops using the provided WritableFile. After this returns, the caller should close the file. On success, the resulting file contains the finalized table.
requirements: Finish() and Abandon() must not have been called prior to this call (REQUIRES comment).
After Finish() returns, the builder stops using the WritableFile passed at construction (per comment).
Caller must check the returned Status to determine success or failure.
If multiple threads may access this TableBuilder and any thread may call a non-const method, callers must use external synchronization (per class-level note).

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::Abandon
functions.description: Discards the table under construction and stops using the provided WritableFile. Use this if the table will not be completed with Finish().
requirements: Finish() and Abandon() must not have been called prior to this call (REQUIRES comment).
If the caller is not going to call Finish(), it must call Abandon() before destroying the builder (per comment).
After Abandon() returns, the builder stops using the WritableFile passed at construction (per comment).
If multiple threads may access this TableBuilder and any thread may call a non-const method, callers must use external synchronization (per class-level note).

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::NumEntries
functions.description: Returns the number of times Add() has been called so far. After a successful Finish(), it reflects the total entries in the finalized table.
requirements: May be invoked concurrently by multiple threads without external synchronization only if no thread may call a non-const method; otherwise, external synchronization is required (per class-level note).

functions.name: leveldb::TableBuilder::FileSize
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the file generated so far. After a successful Finish(), returns the size of the final, generated file.
requirements: May be invoked concurrently by multiple threads without external synchronization only if no thread may call a non-const method; otherwise, external synchronization is required (per class-level note).

functions.name: leveldb::DumpFile
functions.signature: leveldb::Status DumpFile(leveldb::Env* env, const std::string& fname, leveldb::WritableFile* dst);
functions.description: Dumps the contents of a LevelDB storage file to a destination WritableFile in a human-readable, line-oriented text format. The function reads the file named by fname using the provided Env and emits a sequence of newline-terminated records by repeatedly calling dst->Append() for each item discovered in the file. Use this to inspect or diagnose LevelDB files by streaming their textual representation to a writable sink (e.g., a log file or stdout-like wrapper). Returns a non-OK Status if fname is not a LevelDB storage file or cannot be read. Details of the textual format are not specified in this header.
requirements: env must be a valid, initialized leveldb::Env* usable to open and read the target file (inferred from the parameter type and usage).
fname should name a readable LevelDB storage file; otherwise the function will return a non-OK Status (stated in comments).

dst must be a non-null, valid leveldb::WritableFile* that is open and able to accept multiple Append(const Slice&) calls during the dump (stated: the function makes a sequence of dst->Append() calls).

Callers must check the returned leveldb::Status to determine success or failure; on failure, no guarantees about completeness of output are provided (inferred from Status-returning API pattern and partial-output semantics implied by streaming Append calls).
dst must remain valid for the entire duration of the call and should tolerate newline-terminated text records (inferred from streaming behavior).

functions.name: leveldb::Snapshot::~Snapshot
functions.description: Destructor for leveldb::Snapshot. Snapshot is an immutable handle to a particular DB state and is safe for concurrent access. The destructor is protected; clients must not delete Snapshot directly. Snapshots should be released via leveldb::DB::ReleaseSnapshot.
requirements: Do not call the destructor directly; use leveldb::DB::ReleaseSnapshot to release a snapshot.
Any Snapshot pointer passed to ReleaseSnapshot must have been obtained from leveldb::DB::GetSnapshot on the same DB instance.
Callers must not use a Snapshot after it has been released.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::Open
functions.signature: static leveldb::Status Open(const leveldb::Options& options, const std::string& name, leveldb::DB** dbptr);
functions.description: Opens (or creates, depending on options) the database stored at the given path and returns a heap-allocated DB instance via dbptr. On success returns OK and stores a non-null DB*; on error returns non-OK and stores nullptr. Caller owns and must delete the returned DB when no longer needed.
requirements: dbptr must be non-null and point to storage for a DB*.
On success, caller must delete the returned *dbptr when it is no longer needed.
On error, *dbptr will be set to nullptr; callers should check the returned Status before using *dbptr.
The name argument must refer to a valid filesystem path accessible to the process.
Options must be properly initialized; fields such as create_if_missing control creation behavior (details per leveldb::Options, not shown here).

functions.name: leveldb::DB::~DB
functions.description: Virtual destructor for leveldb::DB. Ensures proper cleanup of DB implementations. Iterators and snapshots should be released before the DB is destroyed.
requirements: Callers must not use the DB object after the destructor runs.
All iterators created by this DB should be deleted before the DB is deleted (as noted in NewIterator documentation).
All snapshots acquired via GetSnapshot should be released via ReleaseSnapshot before destroying the DB.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::Put
functions.signature: virtual leveldb::Status Put(const leveldb::WriteOptions& options, const leveldb::Slice& key, const leveldb::Slice& value) = 0;
functions.description: Sets the value for the given key in the database. Overwrites any existing entry for key. Returns OK on success; otherwise a non-OK Status. Consider setting options.sync = true to force write durability.
requirements: key and value Slices must point to valid memory for the duration of the call.
The DB instance must be a valid, open database.
WriteOptions must be initialized; options.sync can be set according to durability needs.
Function may be called concurrently; DB is safe for concurrent access.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::Delete
functions.signature: virtual leveldb::Status Delete(const leveldb::WriteOptions& options, const leveldb::Slice& key) = 0;
functions.description: Removes the database entry for the given key if it exists. Returns OK on success (including when the key did not exist); otherwise a non-OK Status. Consider options.sync = true for durability.
requirements: key Slice must point to valid memory for the duration of the call.
The DB instance must be a valid, open database.
WriteOptions must be initialized.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::Write
functions.signature: virtual leveldb::Status Write(const leveldb::WriteOptions& options, leveldb::WriteBatch* updates) = 0;
functions.description: Applies a batch of updates atomically to the database. Returns OK on success; non-OK on failure. Consider options.sync = true for durability.
requirements: updates must be a non-null pointer to a properly initialized WriteBatch containing the desired operations.
The updates batch must remain valid for the duration of the call.
The DB instance must be a valid, open database.
WriteOptions must be initialized.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::Get
functions.signature: virtual leveldb::Status Get(const leveldb::ReadOptions& options, const leveldb::Slice& key, std::string* value) = 0;
functions.description: Retrieves the value for the given key. On success, stores the value in *value and returns OK. If the key is not found, leaves *value unchanged and returns a Status for which Status::IsNotFound() is true. May return other non-OK statuses on error.
requirements: key Slice must point to valid memory for the duration of the call.
value must be a non-null pointer to an std::string to receive the result.
ReadOptions must be initialized; may specify snapshot/verification options (details per ReadOptions).
Caller should check the returned Status and handle the NotFound case without assuming value was modified.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::NewIterator
functions.description: Creates a new heap-allocated iterator over the DB contents. The iterator is initially invalid; caller must call a Seek method before use. Caller is responsible for deleting the iterator. The iterator should be deleted before the DB is deleted.
requirements: ReadOptions must be initialized; may include a snapshot to read from a stable view.
Caller must delete the returned Iterator when no longer needed.
Do not use the iterator before making it valid via Seek/SeekToFirst/SeekToLast.
The iterator should be deleted before destroying the DB instance that created it.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::GetSnapshot
functions.description: Returns a handle to the current DB state (a consistent snapshot). Iterators created with this snapshot observe a stable view. Caller must later release the snapshot via ReleaseSnapshot.
requirements: Caller must eventually call ReleaseSnapshot with the returned pointer when no longer needed.
The returned Snapshot pointer must be used only with the DB instance that created it.
Snapshot is immutable and thread-safe to read; do not attempt to modify it.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::ReleaseSnapshot
functions.description: Releases a previously acquired snapshot. After this call, the snapshot must not be used.
requirements: snapshot must be a pointer previously returned by GetSnapshot on the same DB instance.
Do not use the snapshot after calling ReleaseSnapshot.
Passing nullptr is not documented as valid; pass only valid snapshot pointers.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::GetProperty
functions.signature: virtual bool GetProperty(const leveldb::Slice& property, std::string* value) = 0;
functions.description: Queries an implementation-defined property of the DB. If the property name is recognized, stores its current value as a string in *value and returns true; otherwise returns false. Recognized properties include leveldb.num-files-at-level<N>, leveldb.stats, leveldb.sstables, and leveldb.approximate-memory-usage.
requirements: property Slice must point to a valid, null-free property name for the duration of the call.
value must be a non-null pointer to an std::string to receive the property value if available.
Caller must handle the false return indicating an unrecognized property name.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::GetApproximateSizes
functions.signature: virtual void GetApproximateSizes(const leveldb::Range* range, int n, uint64_t* sizes) = 0;
functions.description: Estimates the filesystem space used by keys in each of the specified ranges. For each i in [0, n-1], writes the approximate number of bytes used by keys in [range[i].start, range[i].limit) into sizes[i]. Sizes reflect on-disk usage (affected by compression) and may not include very recent writes.
requirements: range must point to an array of at least n Range elements, each with valid Slice start and limit for the duration of the call.
sizes must point to an array of at least n uint64_t elements to receive results.
n must be non-negative; if n is zero, no results are written.
Callers should not assume exactness; values are approximate and may lag recent updates.

functions.name: leveldb::DB::CompactRange
functions.signature: virtual void CompactRange(const leveldb::Slice* begin, const leveldb::Slice* end) = 0;
functions.description: Compacts the underlying storage for the key range [*begin, *end). Discards deleted/overwritten versions and reorganizes data to improve access performance. begin == nullptr is treated as a key before all keys; end == nullptr as a key after all keys. Calling with both nullptr compacts the entire database.
requirements: begin and/or end may be nullptr to denote unbounded ranges; otherwise, they must point to valid Slice objects for the duration of the call.
This operation is typically for advanced users who understand the underlying implementation; it may be expensive.
Function should be called on a valid, open DB.

functions.name: leveldb::DestroyDB
functions.signature: leveldb::Status DestroyDB(const std::string& name, const leveldb::Options& options);
functions.description: Destroys the contents of the database at the given path. Be careful: this irreversibly deletes data. For backward compatibility, if the function is unable to list database files, it may still return Status::OK(), masking that failure.
requirements: name must be a valid filesystem path to a database directory.
Caller must be prepared for data loss; this operation is destructive.
Options must be initialized; any environment/filesystem settings therein will be used.
Caller should check the returned Status, noting that some failures (file listing) may be masked as OK per the comment.

functions.name: leveldb::RepairDB
functions.signature: leveldb::Status RepairDB(const std::string& dbname, const leveldb::Options& options);
functions.description: Attempts to recover as much data as possible from a database that cannot be opened. Some data may be lost; use with caution on important datasets.
requirements: dbname must be a valid filesystem path to a database directory.
Options must be initialized.
Caller should check the returned Status and verify database integrity after repair.
Be aware that repair may lose data and should not be used lightly.

functions.name: leveldb_open
functions.signature: LEVELDB_EXPORT leveldb_t* leveldb_open(const leveldb_options_t* options, const char* name, char** errptr);
functions.description: Opens (or creates, depending on options) a LevelDB database at the given path and returns a handle to it. On failure, returns NULL and sets *errptr to a malloc()-allocated error string.
requirements: options must be a valid, initialized leveldb_options_t pointer (non-NULL).
name must be a non-NULL, null-terminated filesystem path string.
errptr must be non-NULL and satisfy: on entry either *errptr == NULL or *errptr points to a malloc()-allocated, null-terminated error string (on Windows, allocated by this library).
On success, *errptr is left unchanged; on failure, any previous *errptr is freed by the library and *errptr is set to a new malloc()-allocated error message.
All pointer arguments must be non-NULL.

functions.name: leveldb_close
functions.description: Closes a previously opened LevelDB database and releases associated resources.
requirements: db must be a valid, open leveldb_t pointer obtained from leveldb_open (non-NULL).
Must not be called more than once for the same db handle (no double-close).
No other operations should be performed on db after this call.
All pointer arguments must be non-NULL.

functions.name: leveldb_put
functions.signature: LEVELDB_EXPORT void leveldb_put(leveldb_t* db, const leveldb_writeoptions_t* options, const char* key, size_t keylen, const char* val, size_t vallen, char** errptr);
functions.description: Writes a key/value pair into the database (inserts or overwrites). Synchronous behavior is controlled by write options.
requirements: db must be a valid, open leveldb_t pointer.
options must be a valid, initialized leveldb_writeoptions_t pointer.
key must point to a buffer of length keylen; key must be non-NULL and keylen specifies its exact length (binary keys allowed).
val must point to a buffer of length vallen; val must be non-NULL and vallen specifies its exact length (binary values allowed).

errptr must follow the error parameter contract: non-NULL; on entry either *errptr == NULL or points to a malloc()-allocated error string; on failure, the library frees the old value and sets *errptr to a new malloc()-allocated message; on success, *errptr is unchanged.
All pointer arguments must be non-NULL.

functions.name: leveldb_delete
functions.signature: LEVELDB_EXPORT void leveldb_delete(leveldb_t* db, const leveldb_writeoptions_t* options, const char* key, size_t keylen, char** errptr);
functions.description: Deletes the entry for the specified key from the database (writes a deletion).
requirements: db must be a valid, open leveldb_t pointer.
